transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess… I’m here because I keep getting startled. Like, a breaker snaps or a tool drops, or someone walks up behind me, and I just jump. My heart keeps pounding after, even when everybody else has already moved on.
Is there something specific that you think is causing you to be startled, or is it just the sudden noise?

It’s… not just the noise. Sometimes out of nowhere I’ll see that flash again, or hear him yelling. Even if I’m just loading tools in the truck. It kind of knocks me sideways, like I’m right back there.
What is it that you see in that flash?
Just… that flash. Like it’s in my head again. And sometimes I hear the trainee yelling, real sharp. I can be doing something normal, loading tools, and then it’s like I’m back in it for a second.
Was there a specific event that happened involving a trainee and a situation that's connected to these flashes you're experiencing?

Yeah… there was something with a trainee. I don’t really like getting into it, but since then it’s like… I’ll be doing something normal, loading tools in the truck or whatever, and out of nowhere I see that flash in my head, or hear him yelling. Just for a second it feels like I’m back there.
Can you tell me what happened with the trainee that's been causing these flashes?

I… I don’t really want to go through the whole thing. I try not to talk about that day. I make excuses to stay away from certain panels or breakers, certain job sites too, because once it gets started in my head… I can’t shut it off.
You mentioned making excuses to stay away from certain panels or breakers, can you tell me more about what you're trying to avoid?

Mostly those electrical panels, breakers… places that remind me of it. Certain job sites too. I’ll say I’m busy or that somebody else should take it. And I don’t like talking about that day, because once it gets going in my head, I can’t really stop it.
How long have you been experiencing these flashes and startle responses?
Since that arc-flash accident on the retrofit job… so, about a year and a month now. It’s been there pretty much since then.
Are there any other activities or situations that you've been avoiding since the accident?

Yeah… I avoid certain job sites if I can. Panels, breakers, anything like that. I’ll make excuses, say I’m tied up or somebody else knows it better.

And… I don’t like talking about that day. Once it starts in my head, it’s hard to shut it off.
Are you also avoiding people or specific social situations since the accident?

Not really people, I guess… more places and stuff at work. Panels, breakers, certain job sites. I’ll make excuses so I don’t have to go near them. And I try not to talk about that day, because once it starts in my head, it doesn’t stop easy.
Do you often find yourself thinking that you're to blame for what happened or that you're worthless since the accident?
Yeah… I do. I don’t know about “worthless,” but… I walk around mad and guilty most of the time. Like I failed that kid, and everybody can see it on me.
Do you ever feel like you're outside of your body watching yourself when these flashes happen?
I don’t know… not really like that, I don’t think. It’s more just… I’m back there in my head. Not watching myself from outside.
Do you ever feel numb or disconnected from the world around you when you're not having one of those flashes?

Yeah… I guess. Even when my wife or the kids are messing around, trying to make me laugh, or something goes right at work… it just doesn’t really reach me. Like there’s a wall there. I know I should feel good, but I don’t.
Do you feel guilty most of the time about what happened with the trainee?
Yeah. Most of the time. I keep thinking I failed him… and it’s like everybody can tell just by looking at me.
Has your relationship with your family or friends changed significantly since the accident?

Yeah… it has. My wife says I’m not really there at home anymore. And I don’t see people much.

It’s like everything I do now is just trying to keep from having another… blowup like that day. Work’s noticed too. I’ve been written up, and they took me out of the running for supervisor. So… yeah, it’s changed things.
Do you try to avoid thinking about the arc-flash accident?

Yeah. I try not to let it get going in my head. I’ll make excuses to stay away from certain panels or breakers… certain job sites too. And I don’t really talk about that day if I can help it. Once it starts, I can’t shut it off.
Have you had thoughts of hurting yourself since the accident?
I… I don’t know. I don’t really think about it like that. It’s not something I’ve been wanting to talk about.
Have you had any thoughts of hurting yourself since the accident?
I… I’m not sure how to answer that. I don’t think I’ve, like… made any plan or anything. It’s just not something I really want to get into.
Have you had any thoughts of self-harm or suicide since the accident?
I don’t know… I haven’t really sorted it out in my head. I’m not saying I’ve got a plan or anything. I just… I’d rather not talk about it much.
